requirement.evidence: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause. For purposes of this Division, just cause includes at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause.
requirement.note: At-fault and no-fault causes, the 30 or 60 day notice under Civil Code 1946.1, and the void-notice rule are all stated in §§98.0704, 98.0706 and 98.0706(e).

key_value.evidence: Tenancy means the lawful right or entitlement of a tenant to continuously use or occupy a residential rental property for more than 30 days.
key_value.note: Just cause is required for tenancies, defined as more than 30 days.

effective_date.evidence: (“Just Cause Required for Termination of Tenancy” added 5-25-2023 by O-21647 N.S.; effective 6-24-2023.)

status.evidence: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause.
status.note: The document presents the rule as current law and shows no repeal.

coverage.evidence: (k) housing that has been issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, unless the housing is a mobilehome; and
coverage.note: The 15-year certificate-of-occupancy exemption is supported. The 'owner_based_exemption_max_units: 2' value is a loose paraphrase. The document says a landlord-occupant who rents no more than two bedrooms or two ADUs/JADUs is exempt, and a property with two dwelling units is exempt if the landlord occupies one. It does not state a 2-unit cap for owners as such.

citation.evidence: §98.0704 Just Cause Required for Termination of Tenancy
citation.note: The section and both ordinances (O-21647, amended by O-21769) match the document.

requirement.evidence: (i) Unless section 98.0706(c)(1)(A)(ii) applies, the direct payment to the tenant shall be in an amount equal to two months of actual rent under the tenant’s lease in effect at the date of the notice.
requirement.note: The 2 or 3 month amounts, the waiver option, and the lack of any income or tenure condition are supported. 'Must pay a direct payment within 15 days of the notice' is only partly right. The 15 days appears as a required statement in the notice when the landlord elects direct payment, not as a stand-alone duty.

key_value.evidence: (ii) If the tenant is a senior or disabled, the direct payment to the tenant shall be in an amount equal to three months of actual rent under the tenant’s lease in effect at the date of the notice.
key_value.note: Two months is the base amount, per (c)(1)(A)(i).
